implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments and operational processes, with due regard to other requirements such as security. It includes all the design elements needed to define or refine the statistical products or services identified in the business case. This phase specifies all relevant metadata, in accordance with the standards and corporate policies, ready for use later in the business process, as well as quality assurance procedures. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration and whenever improvement actions are identified in the Evaluate phase of a previous iteration. Design activities make substantial use of international and national standards in order to reduce the length and cost of the design process, and enhance interoperability, comparability, etc. Organisations may reuse or adapt design elements from existing processes and consider geospatial aspects of data in the design to enhance the usability and value of the statistical information. Additionally, outputs of design processes may form the basis for future standards at the organisational, national or international levels. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, and operational processes—with a strong emphasis on automation, AI-powered tools, and digital interoperability. Automated and AI-driven processes play a central role in drafting specifications, aligning with corporate and international standards, generating and enriching metadata, simulating system interactions, and iterating design improvements. All statistical products and their supporting metadata are produced in standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable forms, ensuring they are interoperable and reusable across downstream tools, APIs, and organizational systems. Staff are freed from repetitive and routine design work and instead focus on innovation, calibration, and optimizing for evolving user and stakeholder requirements. Design activities thus promote efficiency, quality, and discoverability, embedding best practices for automation, standardization, and open data access. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, can occur in parallel, and may be iterative. Iteration between Design and Build phases is supported through automated versioning and process enhancements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The phase now requires 'automation and AI' for drafting, standards synthesis, metadata creation, and versioning; all outputs must be 'richly described, and machine-actionable,' and staff must be adept at reviewing and contextualizing automated design outputs. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' is core to this, as their work includes 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' and 'provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata.' Their work will now focus less on manual documentation/metadata production and more on reviewing, adapting, and improving AI/automation-generated metadata and outputs, driving digital transformation and interoperability.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design outputs and dissemination
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products, and services to be produced, including all systems, tools, and procedures to be used in dissemination. Automated and AI-supported solutions are used wherever possible to produce initial output templates, align with existing standards, generate metadata, and configure dissemination tools, allowing staff to focus on innovative features and context-specific requirements, including confidentiality. All outputs and dissemination artifacts must be standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable, with support for APIs, comprehensive metadata tagging, and open formats to maximize interoperability, discoverability, and reusability by human and machine clients. The process includes an explicit, early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations, with the expectation that only those genuinely required for user value or compliance are designed—allowing exclusion where end-users can self-serve or alternatives suffice. Outputs may also be designed in partnership with external organizations, ensuring full alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Digital automation, standards, and metadata-rich, machine-actionable products are now required. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer''s focus on 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' as well as contributing to 'documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals,' is reoriented toward the oversight of automation-driven, standards-based design outputs, ensuring discoverability, API compatibility, and proper metadata linkage in digital dissemination environments.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design variables
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables that will be derived from them in sub-process 5.5 (Derive new variables and units), and any statistical or geospatial classifications that will be used. This is also where unit types (including observation units and statistical units) can be designed. It is expected that existing national and international standards will be followed wherever possible. This sub-process may need to run in parallel with sub-process 2.3 (Design collection), as the definition of the variables to be collected and the choice of collection instruments may be inter-dependent to some degree. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument and any that will be derived for analysis or dissemination, with a strong emphasis on standards compliance, automation, and machine-actionability. All variable definitions and supporting metadata must comply with national and international standards (e.g., SDMX), structured in machine-actionable formats and managed through prescribed data management tools (such as Aria or Colectica) to ensure robust lifecycle control and digital traceability. AI/LLM-enabled tools are used to generate, refine, and validate variable names, descriptions, and attributes, maximizing clarity, standardization, and discoverability. Staff involved in this sub-process are proficient in digital metadata standards and tooling, ensuring all variable-related products are interoperable, automation-ready, and reusable by both human and machine users. This ensures that the resulting statistical outputs are consistently described, easily found, and seamlessly integrated across digital platforms and systems.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The need for 'full standards compliance (SDMX and prescribed tools),' 'AI/LLM-enabled tooling for the automated generation, refinement, and validation of variable descriptions and attributes,' and staff 'proficiency in digital metadata standards and tooling' puts the 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' in a central position: 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' The officer's expertise is now directed at supervising AI generation of variable descriptions and ensuring standards and metadata completeness in digital repositories, and documenting/validating digital variable management.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise collection
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing. It may include manual or automatic data capture, for example, using clerical staff or optical character recognition tools to extract information from paper questionnaires, or converting the formats of files or encoding the variables received from other organisations. It may also include analysis of the metadata and paradata associated with collection to ensure the collection activities have met requirements. In cases where there is a physical collection instrument, such as a paper questionnaire, which is not needed for further processing, this sub-process manages the archiving of that material. When the collection instrument uses software such as an API or an app, this sub-process also includes the versioning and archiving of these. The data could be pseudonymised at this stage before further processing.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing, powered by AI/ML-driven validation and enrichment routines to ensure all metadata repositories and IM tagging are complete, current, and machine-actionable. Routine automatic checks identify and close metadata gaps, verify data structure and governance needs, and prepare files for downstream processing. Finalization is continuously informed by internal and external research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and evidence-based best practices—enabling iterative improvement and world-leading quality assurance. The subject matter sponsor holds sole responsibility for certifying and accepting the finalized collection data, while operational staff focus on automation, routine execution, and surfacing improvement ideas and lessons learned. Archiving, versioning, and legal compliance handling are embedded as standard, digital-first procedures, ensuring data and metadata are always audit- and analysis-ready.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Collection finalization must now feature 'automated and AI/ML routines for validating and enriching metadata,' operate as an 'iterative, innovation-driven step,' and assign the subject matter sponsor as responsible for certification/acceptance. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer'—who is responsible for 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' 'providing input to reports for clients and management,' and 'compiling information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata'—will now handle/validate automated QA and AI-enriched metadata at finalization, advise on iterative improvements, and oversee digital processes for collection certification. Their domain expertise now shifts even more toward review, innovation recommendations, and improving automated QA effectiveness.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise data files
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process brings together and finalizes the results of all previous sub-processes in the phase, producing data files (micro- or macro-level) in fully standardized, open, and machine-actionable formats by default. All datasets and supporting documentation are versioned, digitally logged, and immediately available for reproducible handoff to subsequent analysis or dissemination phases. Technical staff ensure compliance with standards and continuous skills development, and all processes are supported by automated documentation and audit trails, supporting immediate traceability, interoperability, and readiness for deployment across business domains.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: All finalized datasets must be 'fully standardized, open, machine-actionable,' with 'automated logs and audit trails, and outputs compatible with human and machine consumers.' The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer'—who 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' and 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine where updates are required...'—is critically involved to ensure metadata compliance, documentation, and integrity of all final datasets, and to facilitate automated transfer to next processes.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Update output systems
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' ('prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.') will take primary responsibility for metadata completeness, tag consistency, and API-readiness at the point of output system update.
